Definition: from G5259 and G3306; to stay under (behind), i.e. remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere:--abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind.
BiblicalUsage: hypoménō is how Scripture says to remain, to endure, to stay under. In Matthew 10:22, the text says "but he that endureth to the end shall be saved." In Mark 13:13, the text says "but he that shall endure unto the end."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, hypoménō is a reminder that perseverance is holding on when holding on is hard — and God holds on to us first. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
